items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I went and read James Joyce over again, because I had read him when I was in English, because that was my major you know.

ctx.x: Maybe that’s why a writer, I think it was Time magazine called you “The James Joyce of Jive.”

I was so flattered by that. I went and read James Joyce over again, because I had read him when I was in English, because that was my major you know. And I had heard Joyce like you know, kind of half an eye on it you know. Because I was always trying to write tunes © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

and think of tunes. And I didn’t pay that much attention. But when that man said that about me in Time magazine, I went back and read James Joyce and I see why he saw fit to do that. Because Joyce used language the way jazz players used the songs they played and the point of departure. He took language and departed into whole worlds of words.
